verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but the price and the data access behind them are assumptions I could not check. A daily forecast pack for one hospital costs about 339 toman (about $0.0013) to produce and the GPU is almost idle (the base case uses about 0.6% of one node at month 24 [D]); the cost is the team and the hospital integration work, not compute. Revenue per hospital is about 52.75M toman a month ($198.84) against 447.85M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 9 paying hospitals [D]. The base case (15 hospitals at month 12, 60 at month 24) breaks even in month 9, with a peak cash need of 2,237M toman (about $8,433) and +2,353M a month at month 24; the conservative case (5 / 20) breaks even in month 15 with a peak cash need of 4,206M and +486M at month 24 (cumulative cash −1,732M, so not paid back); the optimistic case (40 / 150) breaks even in month 5 with +6,555M. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30%, halving customers or doubling integration support keeps break-even between month 10 and 13. What decides it is outside the model: I found no price for hospital software in Iran or abroad (the foreign tools are all quote-based), no evidence that hospitals can export bed and stock data in a usable form, and no count of hospitals willing to buy; 60 hospitals is 5.4% of the 1,117 hospitals in one undated table. Persian narrative quality from an 8B model was not tested. Hospital counts are hypotheses [A]. Tags: [S] sourced, [D] derived and recomputed by code, [A] assumption.

r: (a) Private hospitals and charity hospitals, core by willingness to buy. (b) Hospitals owned by social-security, military and corporate bodies. (c) Hospital groups and university hospital networks, core by revenue. Public hospitals under the universities of medical sciences are the biggest group by count but buy through university procurement [A]. Pool: one table lists 1,117 hospitals and 130,912 beds in Iran: 749 hospitals (90,003 beds) under the universities of medical sciences, 166 private (16,626 beds), 73 social-security (10,853), 32 military (2,190), 37 charity (4,198), 17 Revolutionary Guard (2,483), 9 oil-company (967) and 34 other (3,592), with 402,123 staff (BMC Health Services Research, table 2 of article 10.1186/s12913-021-07164-y, bmchealthservres.biomedcentral.com, read 26 Oct 2026 [S]; the table gives no year and the article is from 2021, so the data are older). Bed density was 1.6 per 1,000 people in 2017 (CIA World Factbook via IndexMundi, updated 18 Sep 2021, read 26 Oct 2026 [S]). At month 24 the base case has 60 hospitals or groups, 5.4% of 1,117 [D]; the conservative case has 20 (1.8%) and the optimistic case 150 (13.4%) [D].

Each morning the hospital gets a 7-day forecast of admissions, discharges and bed occupancy by ward, a list of supplies and drugs likely to run short, and a short Persian narrative for the ward managers, built from the daily census and stock records the hospital already keeps. The labour replaced is a nurse manager and a store keeper compiling the census and supply orders by hand: 45 minutes a day [A], about 107,267 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). A per-pack comparison with that labour is not meaningful, because the plans are priced against a hospital's budget, not against that time. Budget anchor: the table gives 3.07 staff per bed [D: 402,123 ÷ 130,912]; a 70-bed small hospital then has about 215 staff and a payroll of about 5.9B toman a month at the minimum wage, and a 200-bed hospital about 614 staff and 16.9B [D]; the plans at 25M and 60M toman a month are 0.42% and 0.36% of those payrolls, which are floors, so the true share is lower [D]. Foreign anchors: LeanTaaS, Qventus, Hospital IQ, TeleTracking and GE HealthCare Command Center are all enterprise or quote-based with no public price (aiopsschool.com, Top 10 AI Hospital Bed Demand Forecasting Tools, read 26 Oct 2026 [S]), so there is no price anchor and the plan prices are assumptions. Context: Persian press runs stories of searching Tehran for a free ICU bed (Taadol newspaper headline, undated, page blocked [S, headline]).

Direct sales to hospital managers and finance directors; pilots on one ward; hospital-software vendors that already hold the information-system integration; university hospital networks and private hospital groups.
A 60-day pilot on one ward with a published forecast error; a named integration engineer per 10 hospitals [A]; monthly accuracy report. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly subscription by hospital size: Small (up to 100 beds) 25,000,000 toman (about $94), Medium (100–300 beds) 60,000,000 (about $226), Large or a 5-hospital group 180,000,000 (about $678) [A, no price was found]. Mix 55% / 35% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 52,750,000 toman a month (about $198.84) [D]. The Doc 1 pricing note says project; I model it as a subscription so it can be compared with the other services, and an upfront project fee would change cash timing.

Time-series forecasting code (CPU) with a fixed daily pipeline from the hospital's information system; an 8B-class instruction model for the Persian narrative; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 integration engineer and a hospital operations adviser at 50M gross a month [A].

Connecting to each hospital's records, cleaning daily census and stock data, calibrating ward-level models, measuring forecast error against actual occupancy, supporting store keepers and ward managers.
Domestic GPU/cloud host; hospital information-system vendors; payment gateway or bank transfer (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); a hospital operations adviser.

Fixed: team 239.85M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 integration engineer at 45M + 50M adviser, gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 447.85M toman a month (about $1,688) [D]; one-time setup 400M [A] (pipeline tooling and pilots). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 50 toman per pack for storage and alerts [A], an extra integration engineer per 10 hospitals [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity (not reached).
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 integration engineer at 45M + 50M adviser, gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026

[A] the forecasts run on CPU and cost no GPU time; the narrative is about 1,500 tokens in and 700 out [A], 1.0 s at 2,658.57 tokens a second [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B] × 0.8 [A], rounded up
[A] packs are produced in the early morning, so load is bursty
[D] 100% use [A] of the 30 / 30 / 150 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node could serve about 9,969 hospitals at this usage [D: 518,400 ÷ (42 + 10 free-trial packs)], so GPU is never the constraint and the node is 33.5% of fixed cost [D: 150M ÷ 447.85M]; a CPU-only deployment at the 17M toman server price used in earlier services would cut about 133M a month [D], but it was not used because the narrative needs a model server. Integration support at one engineer per 10 hospitals costs 5.5M toman a month per hospital [D: 45M × 1.23 ÷ 10], 10.5% of revenue per hospital; that is the main cost that scales, and real integration work with older information systems may cost more. Gross margin is near 99% only because the plan price is far above compute cost, so it says nothing about whether hospitals will pay that price.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 9 paying hospitals on the fixed-cost formula [D: 447.85M ÷ (52,750,000 × 0.99 − 42 × 50) = 8.6], and stepping through hospital counts with the node and integration hires each needs also gives 9 on one node [D]. Hospitals ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 400M setup falls in month 1.

Hospital counts are [A]. At month 24 the base case is about 60 hospitals or groups producing 2,520 packs a month [D: 60 × 42], which is 0.5% of one node's capacity. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −1,732M toman in the conservative case, +15,336M in the base case and +54,944M in the optimistic case [D]; the peak cash need came earlier in each, and the conservative case has not repaid its cash need by month 24.

r: Integration support doubled (one engineer per 5 hospitals)

sensitivities.x: Every stress keeps break-even within 13 months, which shows the cost side is robust; it does not test the revenue side, because the same plan prices and the same buying decision sit under every row. The last row is an extra stress I added for the integration work. Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 2.5% monthly churn [A, hospital contracts are sticky once integrated] lifetime value per hospital is about 2,089M toman, about $7,874 [D: (52,750,000 × 0.99 − 42 × 50) ÷ 0.025], and holding 60 hospitals needs about 1.5 new hospitals a month [D: 60 × 0.025]. With 40M of marketing and about 5.25 gross additions a month at month 24 [D: 3.75 net + 1.5 replacements], the implied marketing cost per hospital is about 7.6M toman (about $29) [D], which is far too low for hospital sales and should be treated as an understatement.

risks.x: Price: with no price anchor at home or abroad, the plans (0.36–0.42% of a minimum-wage payroll) could be wrong by a large factor in either direction; a hospital buys only if forecasts save more than the fee, and I found no evidence on forecast accuracy for Iranian hospitals.

Data access: forecasts need daily census, discharge and stock records; older hospital information systems may not export them, and I found only academic titles on the quality of those systems, not their content.
Long sales cycles: public hospitals buy through university procurement, and a 6-to-12-month cycle would delay the ramp assumed here; the 60-day pilot also needs staff time from the hospital.
Public hospitals dominate the pool (749 of 1,117 [S]), but they may be the hardest to sell to, so the reachable pool may be nearer the 166 private and 37 charity hospitals [D: 203].
Persian output: the narrative from an 8B model was not tested for correct medical and supply terms; a larger model would raise GPU cost, but the GPU-doubling row shows the cost side can absorb that.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: Any price for hospital capacity or supply-forecasting software, in Iran or abroad (the foreign vendors are quote-based).
The current number of hospitals and beds and the year of the 1,117 / 130,912 table, and how many hospitals can buy independently.
Hospital information-system coverage and whether census and stock data can be exported daily.
Forecast accuracy on Iranian hospital data, and the savings a hospital gets from a better forecast.
Public procurement rules and approval times for university-owned hospitals.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 26 Oct 2026.

The base case breaks even in month 11 and earns +2,337M toman a month (about $8,809) at month 24 with 10,000 paying students, about 1.0% of the 957,798 people registered for the 2025 Konkur [S, D]. r: (a) Students preparing for Konkur and their parents, who pay, core by willingness to buy. (b) Konkur coaching institutes that resell seats to their classes. (c) Grade 11 and 12 students outside the exam year, who use it for school exams [A]. Pool: 957,798 candidates registered for the first round of the 2025 Konkur (Tehran Times, news/512513, 2 May 2025; the article says registered, not that all sat the exam [S]). The base case reaches 10,000 paying students at month 24, 1.04% of that figure [D]; the conservative case 3,000 (0.31%) and the optimistic case 25,000 (2.61%) [D]. These student counts are [A]; no sourced count of paying online students exists in this document.

A tutor in Persian that explains a Konkur question step by step, checks the student's own attempt, makes a weekly study plan, and for Premium adds a weekly 10-minute call with a human tutor. An account is one teacher or one school pack, so the share of teachers reached is higher than these ratios when packs are counted. The counts are [A].

The teacher pastes a textbook chapter or picks a lesson and gets a quiz or exam in Persian with multiple-choice and short-answer questions, an answer key, difficulty levels and a Word or PDF file ready to print. The plans work out at 2,250, 1,467 and 1,200 toman a set, 2.1%, 1.4% and 1.1% of that loaded labour cost [D]. cost_model.x: One node serves about 2,035 accounts including 5 free trial sets each [D: 216,575 ÷ (101.4 + 5)], so nodes rise with the base: 1 at month 12 and 3 at month 24 in the base case, 9 in the optimistic case [D]. The first node is 28.8% of fixed cost [D: 150M ÷ 520.95M]. School packs are 10% of accounts but 59% of sets [D: 100 ÷ 169 per account at full quota], so a few heavy packs drive GPU cost and the pack price needs watching. The 2.99 seconds per set comes from a throughput proxy on an 8B model scaled down for a larger one.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 2,207 paying accounts on the fixed-cost formula [D: 520.95M ÷ (240,000 × 0.99 − 101.4 × 15) = 2,206.7], and stepping through account counts with the nodes each needs gives 2,973 on 2 nodes [D]. Accounts ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 200M setup falls in month 1.

Account counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −8,392M toman in the conservative case (its peak cash need is the month-24 figure because it never turns profitable), −929M in the base case and +15,349M in the optimistic case [D]. The base case has not repaid its cash need by month 24, so the 24-month return is negative even though the run rate is positive.

sensitivities.x: Both cost and revenue stresses push break-even to month 23 or 24 and erase almost all month-24 profit, so the base case has little margin for error. Doubling the GPU price hurts here because School pack users generate many sets. At 8% monthly churn [A, teachers keep a tool through the school year] lifetime value per account is about 2.95M toman, about $11.12 [D: (240,000 × 0.99 − 101.4 × 15) ÷ 0.08]. Holding 6,000 accounts needs 480 replacements a month and the ramp adds 250 [D], so 730 gross additions a month at month 24; with 150M of marketing that is about 205,479 toman (about $0.77) per account [D], which is low and probably an understatement.

risks.x: Willingness to pay: teachers in Iran earn modest pay and free tools exist; no price for a Persian teacher tool was found, and the plans are assumptions.
Question quality: a 14B-class model was not tested on Persian exam questions with correct keys; a wrong key damages a teacher's standing with students.
Free foreign tools: MagicSchool has a free plan with 80+ tools; whether it handles Persian well was not verified, and it may be hard to pay for from Iran.
Textbook and content rights: using chapter text from state textbooks was not verified.
Heavy School-pack use: packs create 59% of sets, so a price or quota error there moves GPU cost.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable-thin on the numbers, with no demand evidence. The base case breaks even in month 14 with 15 paying accounts and earns +900M toman a month (about $3,392) at month 24 with 60 accounts, where an account is a department, faculty or institution [D]. The conservative case (15 accounts) never breaks even and loses 90M a month. All account counts are assumptions. The product sells to universities and schools, which buy slowly, and I found no Iranian price, no accuracy test of automated grading in Persian, and no evidence that universities accept machine-assisted grades.

r: (a) University departments and faculties with large first-year courses and written exams, core by willingness to buy. (b) Private schools and tutoring institutes that grade short-answer homework. (c) Language centres [A]. Pool: about 3,375,000 university students in 2019 and 142 public universities (Iranian Science Center page, isc.ac, undated, read 27 Oct 2026 [S]); the page gives no private-university count, and the figure is older. The accounts here are departments or faculties, not students, so the base case of 60 accounts is not a share of 3,375,000 students [D]; with 142 public universities it is about 0.4 accounts per public university [D]. The counts (4 / 15 conservative, 15 / 60 base, 40 / 200 optimistic at month 12 / 24) are [A].

The teacher uploads student answers (typed or photographed) and a rubric; the tool gives each answer a draft score with a short written feedback in Persian and flags answers where it is unsure, so the teacher only reviews flagged ones. The labour replaced is a grader marking one short essay: 6 minutes [A], about 14,302 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 3,500, 3,000 and 2,500 toman a graded answer, 24.5%, 21.0% and 17.5% of that loaded labour cost [D]. Foreign anchor: Gradescope lists $1 to $3 per student, with institutional quotes in that range (toolsforhumans.ai, undated, read 27 Oct 2026 [S]; the page contradicts itself on which plan has AI grading), which is 265,295 to 795,885 toman per student [D]; the unit differs from a graded answer, so no direct comparison is made. No Iranian price was found.
Direct sales to department heads and deans; pilots on one course; university research-and-innovation offices; private-school owners; conference demos.

A free pilot of 300 graded answers per account with a measured agreement against the teacher's own scores [A]; 1 support person per 40 accounts [A]; a monthly report on score agreement. Priced in toman and indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly subscription by volume: Department (1,000 answers) 3,500,000 toman (about $13.19), Faculty (6,000) 18,000,000 (about $67.85), Institution (40,000) 100,000,000 (about $376.95) [A, no price was found]. Mix 50% / 35% / 15% [A] gives ARPU 23,050,000 toman a month (about $86.88) [D]. Accounts use 70% of their quota [A]. The Doc 1 pricing note says per student; I model volume plans so they compare with other services.

A 14B-class instruction model for scoring and feedback on a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); handwriting and photo reading; 2 engineers at 50M each, 1 support person at 25M and 40M of an assessment adviser, gross [A].
Calibrating scoring against teacher scores per course, building rubric templates, measuring agreement, handling handwritten and photographed answers, supporting academics through pilots.
Domestic GPU/cloud host; a payment gateway or bank transfer (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); university course leaders who lend rubrics and sample scripts; an assessment adviser.

Fixed: team 202.95M toman a month ((50M + 50M + 25M + 40M) gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 60M = 430.95M toman a month (about $1,624) [D]; one-time setup 300M [A] (about $1,131). cost_model.x: One node serves about 85 accounts including 300 free pilot answers each [D: 535,067 ÷ (6,020 + 300)], so the base case needs one node through month 24 and the optimistic case needs 3 [D]. The node is 34.8% of fixed cost [D: 150M ÷ 430.95M]. Gross margin above 90% shows that compute is not the constraint; the constraint is whether departments pay. The 1.45 seconds per answer comes from a throughput proxy on an 8B model scaled down for a larger one, and handwriting reading would add cost that was not modelled.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 19 paying accounts on the fixed-cost formula [D: 430.95M ÷ (23,050,000 × 0.99 − 6,020 × 20) = 19.0], and stepping through account counts with the node each needs also gives 19 on one node [D]. Accounts ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 300M setup falls in month 1.

Account counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −6,976M toman in the conservative case (its peak cash need is the month-24 figure because it never turns profitable), +2,100M in the base case and +26,023M in the optimistic case [D]. Nineteen accounts is a small number, but each account is a department that must be sold individually, so the sales cycle is the real limit.

sensitivities.x: Every stress keeps month-24 profit positive and break-even within 19 months, so the cost side is robust; the revenue side rests on the account counts, which are assumptions. At 3% monthly churn [A, institutions renew by term] lifetime value per account is about 756.6M toman, about $2,852 [D: (23,050,000 × 0.99 − 6,020 × 20) ÷ 0.03]. Holding 60 accounts needs 1.8 replacements a month and the ramp adds 3.75 [D], so 5.55 gross additions a month at month 24; with 60M of marketing that is about 10.8M toman (about $41) per account [D], which is low for a university sale and probably an understatement.

risks.x: Acceptance: universities may refuse machine-assisted scores for official grades, which would limit use to practice work and homework; I found no policy on this.
Persian scoring accuracy: a 14B-class model was not tested on Persian essays, handwriting or rubrics; low agreement with teachers would end pilots.
Slow public buying: public universities buy through procurement and budgets, so a 6-to-12-month cycle would delay the ramp.
Price: no price was found at home and Gradescope's per-student price is a different unit; the plans may be wrong by a large factor either way.
Student data: answers are personal data, and a domestic-hosting requirement may apply to universities; I did not verify the rule.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

r: (a) Learners preparing for IELTS speaking for study or migration, core by willingness to buy. (b) Adults and students improving general English. (c) Language institutes that give practice to their classes [A]. A learner speaks for 5 minutes on an IELTS-style question and gets a transcript, band-style scores for fluency, vocabulary, grammar and pronunciation, corrections, and a model answer; the intensive plan adds two full mock tests. verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with an unsourced pool and an academic-integrity risk. The base case breaks even in month 7 and earns +3,509M toman a month (about $13,227) at month 24 with 6,000 active subscribers; the conservative case (1,500) breaks even in month 15 [D]. Subscriber counts are assumptions: I found no count of master's and PhD students in Iran, only an unsourced total of about 3.2 million students in 2023–24. The margin depends on a very low customer acquisition cost, so I added a stress with marketing ten times higher. Universities may treat ghost-written text as misconduct, and the tool must be framed as an editing, structuring and formatting aid. Persian university template rules were not verified.

r: (a) Master's and PhD students writing a proposal or thesis, core by willingness to buy. (b) Final-year undergraduates with a project report. (c) University staff and journal authors preparing papers [A]. Pool: no count of postgraduate students was found; one site gives about 3.2 million students in 2023–24 across all levels, with no source cited (learningmole.com, read 27 Oct 2026 [S]), and the Iranian Science Center page gives about 3,375,000 in 2019 (isc.ac, undated [S]). The share that are postgraduates is not known, so no share of a pool is given. The base case of 6,000 active subscribers at month 24 is [A].

The student pastes notes or an outline and gets a structured proposal or chapter draft in Persian, the university's heading and numbering rules, a table of contents, figure and table captions, Persian and English reference lists in the required style, and a consistent academic tone; a final check lists sections that do not follow the template. The labour replaced is an editor writing or formatting one section: 60 minutes [A], about 143,023 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 11,667, 6,667 and 6,000 toman a task, 8.2%, 4.7% and 4.2% of that loaded labour cost [D]. A Persian article on typing cost (Maktabkhooneh) exists but its page is blocked, so no price per page was read. No Iranian price for AI thesis help was found.

Telegram and Instagram channels for graduate students, university associations, thesis typing and editing offices as resellers, search for Persian academic formatting queries, and a free 5-task trial.

Self-service with university templates; 1 support person per 2,000 subscribers [A]; a template library per university; optional human editor add-on [A]. Priced in toman and indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly subscription for the writing period: Proposal (30 tasks) 350,000 toman (about $1.32), Thesis (120) 800,000 (about $3.02), PhD (300) 1,800,000 (about $6.79) [A, no price was found]. Mix 45% / 40% / 15% [A] gives ARPU 747,500 toman a month (about $2.82) [D]. Subscribers use 70% of their quota [A]. The Doc 1 pricing note says per project; I model a monthly plan with 25% monthly churn [A], which stands for an average project of about 4 months, so that the model compares with the other services.

A 14B-class instruction model for drafting and a rules engine for formatting on a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); a template library of university rules; a reference-style library; 2 engineers at 50M each, 1 support person at 25M and 40M of a Persian academic editor, gross [A].

Collecting and maintaining university format rules, tuning Persian academic tone, building reference handling for Persian and English sources, DOCX export, supporting students near deadlines, marketing in graduate communities.
Domestic GPU/cloud host; a payment gateway (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); typing and editing offices; universities that publish template rules.

Fixed: team 202.95M toman a month ((50M + 50M + 25M + 40M) gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 150M = 520.95M toman a month (about $1,964) [D]; one-time setup 200M [A] (about $754). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 40 toman per task for export and reference checks [A], GPU time per task, and an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.

cost_model.x: One node serves about 2,722 subscribers including 5 free trial tasks each [D: 216,575 ÷ (74.5 + 5)], so the base case needs one node at month 12 and 3 at month 24, and the optimistic case 6 [D]. The first node is 28.8% of fixed cost [D: 150M ÷ 520.95M]. Gross margin above 90% shows that compute is not the constraint; the constraint is whether students pay and whether acquisition is as cheap as assumed. The 3.59 seconds per task comes from a throughput proxy on an 8B model scaled down for a larger one.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 707 paying subscribers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 520.95M ÷ (747,500 × 0.99 − 74.5 × 40) = 706.8], and stepping through subscriber counts with the node each needs also gives 707 on one node [D]. Subscribers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 200M setup falls in month 1.

Subscriber counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −877M toman in the conservative case, +29,844M in the base case and +89,875M in the optimistic case [D]; the conservative case has not repaid its cash need by month 24. The model keeps the subscriber path fixed, and at 25% churn that path needs many gross additions each month (see the sensitivity section).

r: Marketing ten times higher (1,500M a month)

sensitivities.x: The last row is an extra stress I added, because the base case holds 6,000 subscribers at 25% monthly churn [A], which needs 1,500 replacements a month and the ramp adds 250 [D], so 1,750 gross additions a month at month 24. With 150M of marketing that is about 85,714 toman (about $0.32) per subscriber [D], which is far too low for a paid consumer product; at 1,500M it is 857,143 toman (about $3.23) [D], and even then break-even is month 14 and month-24 profit stays positive. Lifetime value per subscriber at 25% churn is about 2.95M toman, about $11.11 [D: (747,500 × 0.99 − 74.5 × 40) ÷ 0.25]. The other stresses keep break-even within 10 months.

risks.x: Academic integrity: universities may penalise text written by AI, and advisers may reject drafts; the product must be positioned as structuring, editing and formatting, and I did not verify any university rule.
Willingness to pay: no price for AI thesis help in Iran was found; students may use free chatbots for drafts and pay only for formatting.
Persian quality and sources: a 14B-class model may invent references or write weak academic Persian; reference checking against real databases was not designed or costed.
Template upkeep: each university and department has its own rules, and keeping them current costs editor time that the 40M editor may not cover.
Churn and acquisition: the project-length use means constant re-acquisition; the marketing stress shows the effect.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

Any price for thesis writing, typing or formatting help (the Persian pages found were blocked).
University rules on AI-assisted writing and on formatting templates.
Persian academic writing quality of a 14B-class model, and reference accuracy.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but demand is the weak point because a free national system already exists. The base case breaks even in month 5 and earns +4,884M toman a month (about $18,410) at month 24 with 3,000 paying accounts; the conservative case (900) breaks even in month 10 [D]. Account counts are assumptions: I found no count of theses, journal submissions or institutions that would pay. IranDoc runs a national plagiarism system that master's and PhD students must pass for proposals (PhD also for dissertations), and a university page calls a related tool free [S]; the product therefore has to sell pre-submission checking, AI-text detection and a report that explains each match, not the certificate itself. The reference corpus (theses, journal articles) is controlled by others and was not verified as licensable. AI-text detection in Persian has no accuracy figure I could source, and false accusations are a legal and reputational risk.

r: (a) Master's and PhD students who want to check a draft before the mandatory national check. (b) Journal editors and publishers: 1,003 DOAJ-indexed Iranian journals in 2025 (tehrantimes.com, read 28 Oct 2026 [S]); the total number of journals was not found. (c) Universities, institutes and private colleges that want their own check or AI-text screening [A]. Pool: no count of annual theses or submissions was found, so no share of a pool is given; 3,000 accounts at month 24 is [A].

Upload a Persian document and get a similarity report against a corpus, with matched sources, paraphrase detection and an AI-text likelihood score, in minutes. The labour replaced is a librarian or editor checking one document by hand: 30 minutes [A], about 71,512 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 25,000, 30,000 and 16,000 toman a check, 35.0%, 42.0% and 22.4% of that labour cost [D]. The free IranDoc tool (tik.irandoc.ac.ir) is the price anchor; its cost to users is not stated on the IranDoc page (read 28 Oct 2026 [S]). A Persian checker, Hamtajoo, is described in an arXiv paper (2112.13742 [S]), so the method is not new.

Graduate student channels on Telegram and Instagram, journal editor networks, direct sales to university libraries and private colleges, and an API for journal management systems [A]. A free 1-check trial.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal and thin. The base case (360 paying accounts at month 24) breaks even in month 14, earns +443M toman a month (about $1,670) at month 24 and is still −156M cumulative; the conservative case (120) never breaks even, and halving customers leaves month-24 profit at +56M [D]. Only the optimistic case (900 accounts) clearly repays its cash need (+10,060M cumulative) [D]. Account counts are assumptions; they share the same unsourced pool of recruiters as the résumé screening service (#61) and I did not net out overlap. Foreign tools are priced for large employers: HireVue is estimated at about $35,000 a year for its entry plan and $50,000 to $100,000 or more for enterprise, and the vendor does not publish prices [S]; that suggests large Iranian employers are the only ones who could pay more than the plans modelled, and I found none to size. Persian voice recognition quality, candidate consent and legal limits on automated screening were not verified.

r: (a) SMEs and shops hiring staff for a few roles. (b) Recruitment agencies running many first-round screens. (c) Large employers and call-centre firms with high-volume hiring [A]. Pool: no count of Iranian employers or recruiters was found; the only volume datum in this document set is about 10,100 job posts a month on one job site (#61, from a 365,000-row JobVision dataset [S]). 360 accounts at month 24 is [A].

A bot contacts each applicant by chat or voice message, asks role-specific screening questions in Persian, checks availability and salary expectation, scores the answers, and books an interview slot in the recruiter's calendar. The labour replaced is a recruiter's 15-minute phone screen [A], 35,756 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 12,000, 10,000 and 8,000 toman a candidate, 33.6%, 28.0% and 22.4% of that cost [D]. Foreign anchor: HireVue about $35,000 a year entry and $50,000 to $100,000 or more enterprise, third-party estimates published 6 Jan 2026 and updated 8 Jun 2026 (pin.com [S]); it is aimed at large employers and does not map onto the small plans here.
Direct outreach to recruiters and HR managers, Telegram and WhatsApp-style bots for candidates, integration with job boards if allowed [A], and a free 1-candidate trial.

Self-service setup of question sets; templates by job family; 1 support person per 300 accounts [A]. Candidates always get the option to talk to a person. Prices in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly plans: SME with 50 candidates 600,000 toman (about $2.26), Agency with 300 candidates 3,000,000 (about $11.31), Enterprise with 1,500 candidates 12,000,000 (about $45.23) [A, no price was found]. Mix 60% / 30% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 2,460,000 toman a month (about $9.27) [D]. Accounts use 70% of their quota [A]. 12% monthly churn [A].

A Persian speech-recognition model and a 14B-class model for the interview dialogue and scoring on a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); a messaging and calendar integration layer; 2 engineers at 50M and 1 support person at 25M, gross [A].
Question-set design per role, Persian dialogue and voice handling, bias and fairness checks, calendar integration, selling to recruiters.
Messaging platforms and SMS providers, calendar tools, a domestic GPU/cloud host, and a payment gateway (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 153.75M toman a month ((50M + 50M + 25M) gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 361.75M toman a month (about $1,364) [D]; one-time setup 150M [A] (about $565). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 600 toman per candidate for messages and calendar calls [A], GPU time, and an added node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 support at 25M, gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026

[A] 3 minutes of voice answers recognised at 46 times real time = 3.9 seconds [S, faster-whisper benchmark on a smaller card, not re-measured]; plus about 6,000 tokens in and 800 out, 6,800 tokens at 2,658.57 tokens a second [S] × 0.8 × 0.55 for a 14B-class model [A] = 5.8 seconds
[D] 70% use [A] of the 50 / 300 / 1,500 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node serves about 421 accounts including 1 free candidate each [D: 79,949 ÷ (189 + 1)], so the base case needs one node through month 24 and the optimistic case 3 [D]. The first node is 41.5% of fixed cost [D: 150M ÷ 361.75M].

revenue.x: Break-even is about 156 paying accounts on the fixed-cost formula [D: 361.75M ÷ (2,460,000 × 0.99 − 189 × 600) = 155.8], and stepping through account counts with support staff and nodes also gives 156 on one node [D]. Accounts ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 150M setup falls in month 1.

Account counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −5,606M toman in the conservative case, −156M in the base case and +10,060M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per account at 12% churn is about 19.35M toman, about $72.94 [D: (2,460,000 × 0.99 − 189 × 600) ÷ 0.12].

sensitivities.x: The base case holds 360 accounts at 12% monthly churn [A], which needs 43 replacements a month and the ramp adds 20 [D], so about 63 gross additions a month at month 24. With 40M of marketing that is about 633,000 toman (about $2.39) per account [D], which is plausible for a B2B product; the weakness is the small revenue per account against 362M of fixed cost.

risks.x: Thin revenue: the base case barely repays its cash need by month 24, and the conservative case does not.
Candidate acceptance: applicants may refuse to talk to a bot, and a poor voice experience loses candidates the employer wants.
Fair hiring and consent: scoring people by a model needs consent, an appeal route and bias testing; Iranian rules were not verified.
Voice quality: the recognition speed and accuracy on phone-quality Persian were not tested; many open Persian models restrict commercial use.
Messaging platforms: access to and cost of messaging channels in Iran may change, and the 600 toman per candidate is an assumption.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian employers running first-round screening, and candidates per month.
Prices of Iranian screening-bot or scheduling tools.
Persian speech recognition quality on phone-quality audio, and commercial licences of models.
Iranian rules on automated candidate scoring.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 28 Oct 2026.

Site counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian plants with rotating machinery that would pay for monitoring (an undated headline mentions 43,000 active industrial units in 2019 [S, eghtesadonline, page blocked, title only]). The service needs vibration sensors that the customer must buy: vendor-blog prices are $150 to $350 for an entry-level wireless sensor, $400 to $800 with FFT, and $900 to $1,800 industrial-rated [S, oxmaint.com, 28 May 2026, vendor blog, unverified]; at 265,295 toman an entry sensor is 39.8M to 92.9M toman [D], about 133 to 310 months of the 300,000 toman a machine subscription here [D]. Wireless vibration and temperature sensors on motors, pumps, fans and gearboxes send readings to the cloud; the tool learns each machine's normal spectrum, flags bearing, imbalance, misalignment and looseness patterns early, and writes a plain Persian work-order suggestion with severity and time left. verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but the demand and the content rights are unproven. The base case (3,000 paying seats at month 24) breaks even in month 5, peaks at a cash need of 1,350M toman (about $5,090) and reaches +59,556M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (900 seats) breaks even in month 9 and ends at +11,155M cumulative; the optimistic case (9,000 seats) breaks even in month 4 and ends at +197,107M [D]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 6, prices 30% lower in month 6, and half the seats in month 7 [D]. The reason is the low unit cost: a question costs about 1,861 toman to serve (about $0.007) against about 47,674 toman of engineer time to find the same clause by hand [D]. Seat counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian engineering firms, factories or engineers who work from standards, so no pool supports them. The larger blockers are rights and quality. ISIRI (INSO) standards are sold documents, and I could not verify whether their text may be indexed and quoted in a commercial product; the Persian answer quality on technical clauses is also untested. Without a licence, the service can only index the customer's own copies and internal manuals, which fits the per-seat model but narrows the pitch.

r: (a) Engineering consultancies, contractors and factories that work to ISIRI, ISO and IEC standards and keep internal procedures and equipment manuals. (b) Quality and safety departments in plants. Seats are bought by the firm. Pool: I found no count of such firms or engineers; the 3,000-seat base case is [A] and is about 100 firms of 30 seats.

An engineer asks a question in Persian or English and gets the clause, the page and the quote, from the standards and manuals the firm has uploaded or licensed, with a link back to the source page. The labour replaced is searching and reading: 20 minutes per lookup [A], which is 47,674 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 15,000, 10,000 and 7,500 toman a question, 31.5%, 21.0% and 15.7% of that cost [D]. Foreign anchor: Glean does not publish prices; a competitor blog reports from about $50 per user per month, minimum 100 to 250 users, a minimum annual contract of about $50,000 to $60,000 and a Vendr median contract of $98,890 a year (eesel.ai, published 1 Oct 2025, edited 5 Oct 2026 [S, third-party estimates]). $50 is about 13,264,750 toman at 265,295 [D].
Direct sales to quality managers and engineering heads, standards-consultancy firms as resellers [A], industrial and engineering conferences, a free 10-question trial per seat.
Self-serve onboarding with document upload; a monthly review of unanswered questions to fix retrieval; 1 support person per 300 seats [A]. Prices in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Per-seat monthly plans: Starter with 100 questions 1,500,000 toman (about $5.65), Pro with 300 questions 3,000,000 (about $11.31), Team with 800 questions 6,000,000 (about $22.62) [A, no domestic price was found]. Mix 45% / 40% / 15% [A] gives ARPU 2,775,000 toman a seat a month (about $10.46) [D]. Seats use 60% of their quota [A], so 171 questions a seat a month [D]. 3% monthly churn [A].

A retrieval pipeline (document parsing with Persian and table handling, embeddings, reranking) and a 30B-class model on GPU nodes at 150M toman a month each [S]; 2 ML engineers at 60M, 1 integration engineer at 50M and 1 support person at 30M, gross [A].
Document ingestion and OCR of scanned standards, citation checking, evaluation on a question set written with engineers, access control per firm, selling and onboarding.
Standards publishers or INSO for a content licence (none confirmed), a domestic cloud host, and a payment gateway (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 246.0M toman a month ((60M + 60M + 50M + 30M) gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), first GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 60M = 474.0M toman a month (about $1,787) [D]; one-time setup 250M [A] (about $942). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 500 toman a question for embeddings and storage [A], and one added GPU node for each 609 seats at 30% utilisation.
[D] (2 ML engineers at 60M + 1 integration engineer at 50M + 1 support person at 30M, gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[A] 4,000 tokens of retrieved context in plus 500 out on a 30B-class model; throughput scaled from 2,658.57 tok/s [S, A6000 vLLM Llama-3.1-8B] × 0.8 × 0.30 [A]
[D] 60% use [A] of the 100 / 300 / 800 quotas, weighted by plan mix
[D] team 246.0M + first GPU node 150M + infrastructure 10M + accounting 8M + marketing 60M

cost_model.x: One node serves about 609 seats including the 10 free trial questions each [D: 110,256 ÷ (171 + 10)], so the base case needs 5 nodes at month 24 and the optimistic case 15 [D, from the model]; in the base case 5 nodes cost 750M toman a month, about 42% of that month's total cost of 1,783M [D: 5 × 150M ÷ 1,783M].

revenue.x: Break-even is about 178 paying seats on the fixed-cost formula [D: 474.0M ÷ (2,775,000 × 0.99 − 171 × 500)], and stepping through seat counts with support staff and node steps gives 179 on 1 node [D]. Seats ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 250M setup falls in month 1.

Seat counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is +11,155M toman in the conservative case, +59,556M in the base case and +197,107M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per seat at 3% churn is about 88.73M toman, about $334 [D: (2,775,000 × 0.99 − 171 × 500) ÷ 0.03].

sensitivities.x: The base case holds 3,000 seats at 3% monthly churn [A], which needs about 90 replacements a month and the ramp adds about 167, so about 257 gross additions a month at month 24 [D]. With 60M of marketing that is about 233,000 toman (about $0.88) a seat [D], very low for a business-to-business sale; the model does not stress marketing, so the base case is likely too favourable. Because the margin is so high, the result depends on seats and content rights far more than on compute.

risks.x: Content rights: standards are copyrighted publications; without a licence from INSO or another publisher the product can index only the customer's own copies and manuals, which may be too narrow for the pitch.

Answer accuracy: a wrong clause cited in a design or an audit is costly; retrieval quality on Persian technical text, tables and scanned pages is unmeasured here, and customers will want exact quotes with page links.
Seat pool: the number of firms that buy per-seat tools for engineers is unknown, and free general assistants compete on the same question.
Data security: factories and defence-linked firms may refuse cloud upload of internal manuals, pushing demand to on-premises installs (see #99), which this model does not price.
Price anchor: the foreign figure is a competitor's estimate of a vendor that does not publish prices; domestic prices were assumed and not tested.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian engineering firms, plants and engineers that work from standards daily.
Whether ISIRI or INSO standards may be indexed, quoted and resold in a commercial product, and at what price; the INSO catalogue figure of more than 14,000 standards is from February 2011.
Persian retrieval and answer accuracy on technical standards, and inference speed on the RTX 6000 Ada for the chosen model.
Willingness to pay per seat; the prices are assumptions.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 28 Oct 2026.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal on the numbers, and the value case rests on energy savings I could not price. The base case (75 paying sites at month 24) breaks even in month 12, peaks at a cash need of 2,392M toman (about $9,017) and reaches +3,491M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (24 sites) reaches break-even only in month 24 and ends at −4,856M cumulative; the optimistic case (180 sites) breaks even in month 7 and ends at +19,763M [D]. Break-even in the base case slips to month 13 with doubled compute prices, month 14 with prices 30% lower and month 17 with half the sites [D]. The plans are priced at 116.5% to 186.5% of the cost of an engineer's hour per daily run [D], so labour saved does not justify them; the service must pay for itself through lower energy bills. At an assumed 5% saving, a Site S plan needs an energy bill of at least 160M toman a month (about $603) and Site L at least 1,000M (about $3,770) to break even for the customer [D], but I could not retrieve Iranian industrial electricity or gas tariffs, so I cannot say how many sites meet that. Site counts are assumptions, with no sourced pool. The savings-share fee named in the service list is not modelled; it is possible upside and would need metering the customer accepts as proof. The model runs on CPU servers, not GPUs.

r: (a) Small sites: greenhouses, workshops and commercial buildings with one or two meters. (b) Mid-size plants with several zones or production lines. (c) Large industrial sites with sub-metering. Pool: I found no count of Iranian sites with smart meters or building-management systems; 75 paying sites at month 24 is [A]. The only sourced figure is a national saving potential of 190 million barrels of oil equivalent a year in Iranian industry (eceee 2014 summer-study paper, undated figure [S]), which gives no per-site number.

The tool reads meter and sensor data, forecasts load, and each day recommends or sends schedules (pump and compressor start times, greenhouse heating and lighting, chiller set-points) that cut peak demand and waste, with alerts when a site drifts from its normal pattern. The labour replaced is an energy engineer reviewing a day of data: 60 minutes [A], 143,023 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 266,667, 200,000 and 166,667 toman a run, 186.5%, 139.8% and 116.5% of that cost [D], so the labour comparison does not support the price and the saving must. No foreign price anchor was found.
Direct sales to plant managers and greenhouse owners, energy-audit consultants as resellers [A], industrial-estate associations, and a free 10-run trial.
Onboarding with a meter-integration engineer; monthly savings report; 1 support person per 20 sites (integration is heavy) [A]. Prices in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly plans per site: Site S with 30 runs 8,000,000 toman (about $30.16), Site M with 100 runs 20,000,000 (about $75.39), Site L with 300 runs 50,000,000 (about $188.47) [A, no price was found]. Mix 50% / 35% / 15% [A] gives ARPU 18,500,000 toman a site a month (about $69.73) [D]. Sites use 90% of their runs [A], so 85.5 runs a site a month [D]. 3% monthly churn [A]. No savings-share fee is included.

A load-forecasting and schedule-optimisation engine on CPU servers (3 servers, 51M toman a month [A, from Arvan EUR54 a month for a 4-vCPU server at 300,000 toman per euro, rounded to 17M each]); 3 engineers at 60M and 1 support person at 30M, gross [A].

Site counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −4,856M toman in the conservative case, +3,491M in the base case and +19,763M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per site at 3% churn is about 607.65M toman, about $2,290 [D: (18,500,000 × 0.99 − 85.5 × 1,000) ÷ 0.03].

risks.x: Unproven savings: the whole case rests on the customer saving more than the fee; the 5% saving used for the check above is an assumption, and a site that has already tuned its schedules saves less.
Tariff structure: how much a shifted load saves depends on Iranian industrial tariffs, subsidies and supply cuts, which I could not retrieve.
Metering and integration: many sites lack interval meters or open interfaces; sensor installation is a hardware and integration cost not in the model.
Control risk: sending schedules to pumps or heaters can disrupt production; customers may accept recommendations only, which weakens the savings.
Savings-share contracts need an agreed baseline; disputes are likely and the revenue is not modelled.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but willingness to pay and diagnosis accuracy are unproven and the revenue per farmer is tiny. The base case (12,000 paying farmers at month 24) breaks even in month 8, peaks at a cash need of 1,989M toman (about $7,499) and reaches +29,029M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (3,000 farmers) breaks even in month 15 but has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −1,223M, about $4,610); the optimistic case (30,000) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +91,357M [D]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 9, prices 30% lower in month 10 and half the farmers in month 12 [D]. Average revenue is only 570,000 toman a farmer a month (about $2.15) [D], so the model needs thousands of paying users, and I found no count of Iranian farmers who would pay for an app; the customer counts are assumptions. Usage is assumed at 50% of quota because disease problems are seasonal, and churn at 8% a month. Accuracy is the central risk: a competitor review says the best-known apps struggle with rare conditions and regional variants and should be treated as screening tools (flypix.ai, 9 Jun 2026 [S]), and I have no Iranian crop-image dataset. The model sends photos to our GPUs; one node serves about 4,700 farmers [D]. Spraying advice for pesticides sold in Iran needs a product list I did not find.

r: (a) Individual farmers and orchardists with a smartphone. (b) Larger growers and greenhouses. (c) Cooperatives and agricultural service offices that buy for their members. Pool: I could not retrieve a count of Iranian agricultural holdings or farmers (the FAO census pages found were old and the Tehran Times greenhouse article was blocked); 12,000 paying farmers at month 24 is [A].

The farmer photographs a leaf or fruit; the tool names the likely disease or pest, gives treatment and prevention steps in Persian, and logs the case by location so co-ops see outbreaks. The labour replaced is an agronomist consultation: 30 minutes [A], 71,512 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 10,000, 6,250 and 6,000 toman a diagnosis, 14.0%, 8.7% and 8.4% of that cost [D]. Foreign anchor: Agrio is freemium with undisclosed prices (flypix.ai, 9 Jun 2026 [S]); I found no published price for Plantix.
Cooperatives and agricultural service offices [A], extension agents, Telegram and Instagram groups of farmers, agri-input shops, app stores (Cafe Bazaar and Myket), and 3 free diagnoses per user.
Self-serve app with a phone-support line for co-ops; seasonal campaigns; 1 support person per 300 customers [A]. Prices in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly plans: Farmer with 20 diagnoses 200,000 toman (about $0.75), Farmer Pro with 80 diagnoses 500,000 (about $1.88), Co-op with 500 diagnoses 3,000,000 (about $11.31) [A, no domestic price was found]. Mix 60% / 30% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 570,000 toman a customer a month (about $2.15) [D]. Users use 50% of their quota [A], so 43.0 diagnoses a customer a month [D]. 8% monthly churn [A]. Store and payment fees 10% of revenue [A].

A crop-disease image classifier fine-tuned on collected Iranian crop images plus an advice generator, on GPU nodes at 150M toman a month each [S]; 2 ML engineers at 60M, 1 agronomist at 40M and 1 support person at 25M, gross [A].

Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 300M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −1,223M toman in the conservative case, +29,029M in the base case and +91,357M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per customer at 8% churn is about 6.25M toman, about $23.56 [D: (570,000 × 0.90 − 43.0 × 300) ÷ 0.08].

Iran's smart-irrigation programme gives context but no saving figure: about 10,000 hectares across 110 pilot projects, with no water-saving number stated (tvbrics.com, undated, read 28 Oct 2026 [S]). Farm counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian farms that would pay. The model runs on CPU servers, not GPUs; sensors, valves and controllers are the customer's cost and are not priced.

I found no count of Iranian couriers, delivery shops or fleets (an AloPeyk page I tried was not retrievable), so customer counts are assumptions. Route quality depends on road, traffic and address data from a domestic map provider, whose price and licence terms I could not find.

The Iranian online travel market is estimated at $2,037.7M in 2025 (IMARC, a vendor estimate, read 31 Oct 2026 [S]); the base case's booked value is about $1.4M a year [D], about 0.07% of that, so scale is not the question; winning the traveller's booking and getting access to supplier availability and prices is. verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with legal and data blockers that the model does not price. The base case (1,200 paying customers at month 24) breaks even in month 8, peaks at a cash need of 1,971M toman (about $7,428) and reaches +18,335M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (400 customers) breaks even in month 15 but is still at -582M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (3,500) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +71,357M [D]. Every sensitivity stays profitable on a monthly basis: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 10, prices 30% lower in month 11 and half the customers in month 13 [D]. ARPU is 2,870,000 toman a month (about $10.82) [D] and lifetime value about 69.8M toman (about $263) [D]. The cost that matters is compute and support together: at month 24 the base case runs 2 GPU nodes (about 33% of that month's cost of 904M) and 6 added support staff (about 24%) [D]. Customer counts are [A]: I found no count of Iranian importers, exporters or customs brokers, so the pool is unsourced. The blockers are (1) tariff-code and duty accuracy, because Iranian duties are a 4% minimum plus a trading profit set by the Council of Ministers and the schedule has 8,357 tariff lines as of 2020 [S], so a wrong code or a stale rate can cost the customer money and the service has no confirmed rate feed; (2) sanctions: the United States keeps comprehensive sanctions on Iran apart from specific licences, and General License X of 22 June 2026 covered only oil, petrochemical and related shipping, insurance and payment transactions and was due to expire on 21 August 2026 [S], so the service must run only on domestic hosting and models, must not draft documents that hide the origin, destination or parties of a shipment, and may be asked by customers to do so; (3) the customer remains legally responsible for the declaration, so liability sits with the user but disputes would reach the provider.

r: (a) Small traders and importers handling about 10 shipments a month (Small trader plan). (b) Trading companies handling about 40 shipments a month (Trader plan). (c) Customs broker offices handling about 200 shipments a month (Broker plan). Pool: no count of commercial-card holders, importers or brokers was found; 1,200 paying customers at month 24 is [A].

For each shipment the service reads the invoice, packing list and bill of lading, proposes the 8-digit tariff code with the matching duty rate and permit requirements, and checks the document set against the 14 documents Iranian import needs (warehouse receipt, commercial and proforma invoices, packing list, delivery order, bill of lading, manifest, certificate of origin, import registration permission, broker licence card, commercial card, power of attorney, inspection certificate, insurance policy) [S, Iran trade regulation guidance 2020]. The labour replaced is a trader or clerk spending 3 hours a shipment on gathering, checking and classifying [A], 429,069 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 100,000, 80,000 and 60,000 toman a shipment, 23.3%, 18.6% and 14.0% of that cost [D]. Duty or delay savings are not priced.
Customs broker associations and trading chambers [A], chat-app support, a web app with document upload, and 1 free shipment per customer.
Self-service upload with a review screen before anything is used; chat support, 1 support person per 200 customers [A]; every proposed code is shown with its reasoning so the user confirms it.

Monthly plans: Small trader 1,000,000 toman (about $3.77) for 10 shipments, Trader 3,200,000 (about $12.06) for 40, Broker office 12,000,000 (about $45.23) for 200 [A, no domestic or foreign price was found]. Mix 55% / 35% / 10% [A] gives ARPU 2,870,000 toman a customer a month (about $10.82) [D]. Customers use 80% of their quota [A], so 31.6 shipments a customer on average [D]. 4% monthly churn [A].

One RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB GPU node at 150M toman a month [S, Sindad, 14 Sep 2026]; a tariff schedule and permit database kept current (source not confirmed); 2 engineers at 60M, 1 customs specialist at 40M and 1 support person at 30M, gross [A].

Document extraction for Persian and English trade documents, tariff-code retrieval and checking, duty-rate updates, permit and document checklists, sanctions screening of the parties and countries named in documents, onboarding and support.

A licensed customs broker for review of disputed codes [A, none confirmed], the owner of tariff and rate data (the customs administration or a data reseller, none confirmed), a domestic cloud host, and a payment gateway (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

Fixed: team 233.7M toman a month ((60M + 60M + 40M + 30M) gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), first GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 441.7M toman a month (about $1,665) [D]; one-time setup 250M [A] (about $942). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, 1,500 toman per shipment for storage and form handling [A], one added GPU node for each 1,193 customers, and one added support person (36.9M toman a month loaded) for each 200 customers.
[D] (2 engineers at 60M + 1 specialist at 40M + 1 support person at 30M, gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[A] 3 documents read by a vision-language model at about 4 s each plus code retrieval and checklist, rounded; no benchmark for Persian customs documents

cost_model.x: One node serves about 1,193 customers including 1 free shipment each [D: 38,880 ÷ (31.6 + 1)], so the base case needs 2 nodes at month 24 and the optimistic case 3 [D, from the model]; in the base case the 2 nodes are about 33% of that month's total cost of 904M [D: 300M ÷ 904M]. The 6 added support staff cost about 221M, about 24% of it [D: 6 × 36.9M ÷ 904M].

revenue.x: Break-even is about 158 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 441.7M ÷ (2,870,000 × 0.99 − 31.6 × 1,500) = 158.1], and stepping through customer counts with support staff and node steps gives 159 on 1 node [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 250M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is -582M toman in the conservative case, +18,335M in the base case and +71,357M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per customer at 4% churn is about 69.8M toman, about $263 [D: (2,870,000 × 0.99 − 31.6 × 1,500) ÷ 0.04]. The Broker plan is 10% of customers [A] but 42% of revenue [D: 1,200,000 of 2,870,000 toman], so a few broker offices decide the result.

sensitivities.x: The base case holds 1,200 customers at 4% monthly churn [A], which needs about 48 replacements a month, and the ramp adds about 75, so about 123 gross additions a month at month 24 [D]. With 40M of marketing that is about 325,000 toman (about $1.23) per customer [D], low for businesses that must trust the tool with customs declarations; the model does not stress marketing, so the base case is likely too favourable.

risks.x: Wrong code or stale duty rate: the schedule has 8,357 tariff lines (2020) and duty includes a trading profit set by the Council of Ministers [S]; a wrong answer costs the customer duty or a penalty. Vendor-reported AI first-pass accuracy of 93-96% against 90-95% for specialist brokers (camtomx.com, undated, vendor [S]) is not Iranian evidence.

Sanctions exposure: Iran remains under comprehensive US sanctions except for specific licences [S, GL X, 22 Jun 2026, expiry 21 Aug 2026, status after that not checked]. The service must use no foreign cloud or model, and customers may ask for documents that conceal parties or origin; screening and refusal rules are a cost and a churn risk.
Data access: no confirmed source for official tariff and rate updates or for permit rules by code.

Broker substitution: customs brokers already prepare declarations and bundle classification in the per-entry fee [S, camtomx.com]; a broker-office plan only works if brokers adopt the tool rather than treat it as a threat.
Liability: the user signs the declaration, but disputes over a suggested code would reach the provider; terms of service and professional insurance are unpriced.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of Iranian importers, exporters, commercial-card holders and customs brokers, and shipments per month (the WCO page of 17 Nov 2017 gives no counts).
Any domestic or foreign price for a tariff-code assistant (the sources found state no prices).
Whether official tariff and duty-rate data can be obtained in machine-readable form, and its licence.
Accuracy of document extraction on Persian customs documents and of code suggestions for Iranian 8-digit codes.
Whether OFAC General License X was extended past 21 August 2026, and how sanctions law applies to each customer's trade.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 31 Oct 2026.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal, and weaker than its headline break-even suggests. The base case (3,500 paying customers at month 24) breaks even in month 13, peaks at a cash need of 2,600M toman (about $9,801) and reaches only +2,515M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (1,000 customers) first shows a profit in month 23 but loses 99M in month 24 when a new GPU node is added and is at -5,317M cumulative [D]; the optimistic case (10,000) breaks even in month 7 and ends at +23,240M [D]. A doubled GPU price or prices 30% lower each push the base case to no break-even within 24 months, and only halving customers still breaks even (month 16) [D]. ARPU is 955,000 toman a month (about $3.60) [D] and lifetime value about 13.2M toman (about $50) [D]. Compute is the cost that matters: gross margin by plan falls from 63.9% to 40.4%, and at month 24 the base case runs 8 GPU nodes, about 46% of that month's cost of 2,581M, plus 14 added support staff, about 20% [D]. Customer counts are [A]: I found no count of Iranian video creators, schools or channels (Aparat reports 60M+ monthly users but no creator count [S]), so the pool is unsourced. The blockers are licence and quality of the speech-synthesis step, because the Persian voice models I found are non-commercial (one CC-BY-NC 4.0, one under the Coqui public licence, which restricts commercial use [S]), and dubbing quality in Persian is unproven. Foreign dubbing tools charge about $0.24 to $2.44 per video minute [S, perso.ai, 23 Oct 2026, vendor page, Persian support not stated], while the plans here are $0.015 to $0.025 a minute; the low price is [A] and is what keeps margins thin.

r: (a) Individual video creators and course sellers (Creator plan). (b) Channels, schools and small media teams (Channel plan). (c) Studios and platforms with large back catalogues (Studio plan). Pool: no creator or channel count was found; 3,500 paying customers at month 24 is [A].

The customer uploads a video; the service returns Persian subtitles with timing, a translation into or out of Persian, and optionally a synthetic dub. The labour replaced is a freelancer spending 5 working minutes per video minute on transcription, timing and proofreading [A], 11,919 toman per minute at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]); dubbing by voice actors is not priced. The plans work out at 6,667, 5,000 and 4,000 toman a video minute, 55.9%, 42.0% and 33.6% of that cost [D].
Creator communities, online-course sellers, school and training-centre sales, a web app, and 10 free minutes per customer.
Self-service upload with a subtitle editor; chat support; 1 support person per 250 customers [A].

Monthly plans: Creator 400,000 toman (about $1.51) for 60 minutes, Channel 1,500,000 (about $5.65) for 300, Studio 6,000,000 (about $22.62) for 1,500 [A, no domestic price was found]. Mix 70% / 25% / 5% [A] gives ARPU 955,000 toman a customer a month (about $3.60) [D]. Customers use 80% of their quota [A], so 153.6 video minutes a customer on average [D]. 6% monthly churn [A].

One RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB GPU node at 150M toman a month [S, Sindad, 14 Sep 2026]; a Persian speech-recognition model (the gooya-v1.4 model scores a word error rate of 14.72 on asr-farsi-youtube against 40.95 for whisper-large-v3 [S, navidved leaderboard, 23 Oct 2026]; its licence was not checked) and a commercially usable voice model (none confirmed); 2 engineers at 60M, 1 Persian linguist at 25M and 1 support person at 30M, gross [A].
Speech recognition and timing, translation quality control, voice synthesis tuning, subtitle editor, queue and storage management, onboarding and support.
A licensed voice dataset or voice actors for a commercial voice (none confirmed), a domestic cloud host, and a payment gateway (worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]).

revenue.x: Break-even is about 560 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 443.25M ÷ (955,000 × 0.99 − 153.6 × 1,000) = 559.8], and stepping through customer counts with support staff and node steps gives 889 on 2 nodes [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 250M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is -5,317M toman in the conservative case, +2,515M in the base case and +23,240M in the optimistic case [D]. Lifetime value per customer at 6% churn is about 13.2M toman, about $50 [D: (955,000 × 0.99 − 153.6 × 1,000) ÷ 0.06]. The Channel plan is 25% of customers [A] and 39% of revenue [D: 375,000 of 955,000 toman]; the Studio plan is 5% of customers but 31% of revenue [D: 300,000 of 955,000], at the lowest margin.

With 60M of marketing that is about 144,000 toman (about $0.54) per customer [D], very low; the model does not stress marketing, so the base case is likely too favourable.

risks.x: Voice licence: the Persian voice models found are non-commercial (CC-BY-NC 4.0 and a Coqui public licence, with conflicting metadata on one [S]); a commercial voice needs a licensed dataset or voice actors, which is unpriced.
Thin margin: GPU time is the main cost and the base case has no cushion against a price cut or a higher compute time per minute [D].

Content liability: a platform that dubs customer videos may be asked to remove or refuse content; no rules were checked.

The base case (600 paying accounts at month 24) breaks even in month 7, peaks at a cash need of 1,695M toman (about $6,389) and reaches +36,372M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (200 accounts) breaks even in month 11 and is at +6,150M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (1,500) breaks even in month 4 and ends at +107,586M [D]. The sensitivities show the exposure: a doubled GPU price means no break-even within 24 months, a peak cash need of 17,778M and a month-24 loss of 1,286M; prices 30% lower break even in month 13 and half the accounts in month 10 [D]. ARPU is 20,300,000 toman a month (about $76.52) [D] and lifetime value about 604M toman (about $2,278) [D]. The base case processes about 19.7M pages a month at month 24 [D], needs 39 GPU nodes, about 77% of that month's cost of 7,616M, while 4 added support staff are about 2% [D]. Enterprise accounts are 5% of customers [A] but 49% of revenue and use 76% of the pages [D], at a gross margin of 29.1% [D]. Account counts and volumes are [A]: I found no count of Iranian developers or back offices that need OCR, so the pool is unsourced. On a public Persian benchmark of 6,669 printed lines and 6,669 handwritten pages [S, Reza2kn dataset, undated, table has copy errors], a 666M-parameter model (Bina 0.1 Koochik) scored a handwriting word error rate of 11.41% and a closed-API model (Gemini 3.5 Flash) 33.95%, while Tesseract scored 89%; the licences of these open models were not stated, so the commercial right to run them is unconfirmed. Google's Enterprise OCR costs $1.50 per 1,000 pages ($0.60 above 5M pages) [S, 24 Oct 2026], against $3.02, $2.26 and $1.51 per 1,000 pages here. ID and card images are personal data, which adds storage and consent duties that I did not research.

r: (a) Developers and small firms adding OCR to an app (Starter plan, about 5,000 pages a month). (b) Back offices, accountants and insurers digitising documents (Business plan, about 50,000). (c) Banks, archives and large back offices (Enterprise plan, about 500,000). Pool: no count was found; 600 paying accounts at month 24 is [A].

An API and web upload return text, layout and fields from Persian printed pages, handwritten pages and ID and bank-card images, with confidence scores. The labour replaced is a clerk typing one page in 15 minutes [A], 35,756 toman a page at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 800, 600 and 400 toman a page, 2.2%, 1.7% and 1.1% of that cost [D].
Developer documentation and sample code, direct sales to back offices and banks [A], reseller integrations with accounting and archive software, and 100 free pages per account.
API keys and a dashboard with usage and confidence reports, integration support, service-level terms for Enterprise; 1 support person per 150 accounts [A].

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: marginal. The base case (600 paying accounts at month 24) breaks even in month 13, peaks at a cash need of 2,758M toman (about $10,396) and reaches only +4,206M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (200 accounts) breaks even in month 19 but is still -4,847M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (1,500) breaks even in month 7 and ends at +26,082M [D]. The sensitivities show little margin: a doubled GPU price means no break-even within 24 months and a month-24 loss of 304M a month; prices 30% lower break even in month 19 with only +84M a month at month 24; half the accounts break even in month 17 [D]. ARPU is 5,400,000 toman a month (about $20.35) [D] and lifetime value about 80.5M toman (about $303) at 6% monthly churn [D]. Break-even needs about 97 accounts [D] because fixed costs of 466.3M toman a month are large against an ARPU this low. Base-case month 24 uses 9 GPU nodes, about 62% of that month's cost of 2,194M, and 5 added support staff, about 8% [D]. Account counts are [A]: I found no count of Iranian SMEs or agencies that would pay for an agent builder. Foreign tools are the reference: Zapier Professional costs $19.99 a month for 750 tasks and $129 for 10,000 [S, toolradar.com, updated 30 Oct 2026], Make from $9 for 10,000 operations [S, same page], and n8n can be self-hosted on a $15-30 VPS [S, same page], so a free self-hosted alternative exists for technical buyers. A run here is not the same unit as a Zapier task, so the price comparison is only approximate [A]. Integrations with Iranian services (payment gateways, messengers, accounting tools) are the product's real moat and cost, and their API access was not verified.

r: (a) Small shops and freelancers automating chat replies and sheet updates (Starter plan, about 2,000 runs a month). (b) Agencies and SMEs running several agents (Pro plan, about 10,000). (c) Larger firms and agencies reselling to clients (Business plan, about 60,000). Pool: no count was found; 600 paying accounts at month 24 is [A].

A visual builder where a non-programmer connects a trigger (message, form, new order), an AI step in Persian, and an action (reply, spreadsheet row, notification), paid in toman. The labour replaced is a staff member doing the same task by hand in 10 minutes [A], 23,837 toman a run at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]). The plans work out at 1,000, 800 and 667 toman a run, 4.2%, 3.4% and 2.8% of that cost [D].

Mix 70% / 25% / 5% [A] gives ARPU 5,400,000 toman an account a month (about $20.35) [D]. Accounts use 75% of their quota [A], so 5,175 runs an account on average [D]. 6% monthly churn [A].

The 5 added support staff cost about 185M, about 8% of it [D: 5 x 36.9M / 2,194M]. The 2.0 seconds a run is an assumption; agent runs with long documents or many tool calls would use more.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 97 paying accounts on the fixed-cost formula [D: 466.3M / (5,400,000 x 0.99 - 5,175 x 100) = 96.6], and stepping through account counts with support staff and node steps gives 136 on 2 nodes [D]. sensitivities.x: The base case holds 600 accounts at 6% monthly churn [A], which needs about 36 replacements a month, and the ramp adds about 38, so about 73 gross additions a month at month 24 [D]. risks.x: Thin margin at scale: ARPU is $20.35 against fixed costs of $1,758 a month, and a 30% price cut leaves only +84M a month at month 24 [D].

Free self-hosted competitor: n8n can run on a $15-30 VPS [S], so technical buyers may not pay.

Foreign unit mismatch: a run is not a Zapier task, so the price comparison is approximate [A].
